title: Notice Windows and Temporary Credit Deadlines for Personal Checking Claims
content:
Each Personal Checking tier sets the number of calendar days after a disputed item posted within which notice of an electronic-transaction claim still qualifies, the number of business days after the notice date by which a temporary credit is owed on a claim still open, and the number of business days used in place of that deadline where the account was opened recently.

| Tier | Calendar days after the item posted within which notice qualifies | Business days after the notice date by which a temporary credit is owed | Business days used instead where the account is inside its new-account period |
|---|---|---|---|
| Access Checking | 120 | 10 | 20 |
| Student Checking | 120 | 10 | 20 |
| Everyday Checking | 120 | 10 | 20 |
| Interest Checking | 120 | 10 | 20 |
| Premier Checking | 120 | 10 | 20 |
| Private Client Checking | 120 | 10 | 20 |

The three settings are the same across every Personal Checking tier. The longer deadline of 20 business days is the one that governs where the account was opened fewer than the 30 calendar days of the tier's new-account period before the notice date.

**Reading the two deadlines (hypothetical).** A claim filed on an account opened 12 calendar days earlier is inside the new-account period, so the temporary credit is owed on the 20th business day after the notice date rather than the 10th. A claim filed on an account opened 200 calendar days earlier is governed by the 10-business-day deadline.
